clips.shorts_title: This Is The Difference Between The Dot-Com Bubble And Today
clips.description: In 1999, when Jeff Bezos announced Amazon would lose more money, the stock soared. Today, investors are terrified of spending. This story reveals the key difference between the dot-com bubble and the current AI revolution.

Now, the risk here is, and, you know, I have an economics background, and I'm always looking for those risks. But I don't think it's going to be for a long time. You need to listen to Elon Musk, who's talking about chips and power as, you know, for as far as the eye can see, being in short supply.

clips.shorts_title: The AI Chip Boom Won't End Like The Dot-Com Bubble
clips.description: During the dot-com bust, we had 'dark fiber'—unused infrastructure. Today's AI boom is different. The GPUs getting installed are 'alive' and in voracious demand, a key reason why a chip glut isn't coming anytime soon.

clips.topic: The Shocking Cost of the AI Arms Race
clips.viral_hook: So I think that the shareholder base holding the MAG-6, they have gotten so used to cash hordes and massive free cash flow generation, that this is a big shock to them, seeing these hyperscalers take their capital spending budgets up 100% in one year.

clips.topic: Why Investors Fear the AI Boom
clips.viral_hook: Many of the most seasoned investors today were very young when the tech and telecom bubble took off. And now they are the gray hairs.
clips.transcript: Many of the most seasoned investors today were very young when the tech and telecom bubble took off. And now they are the gray hairs. And I'm friends with a lot of them. And many of them are saying, been there, done that. I'm leading this organization now, and I'm going to protect it from this bubble. And we understand that. But as I just described, we have really just started this journey. And we expect the capital spending cycle to go much further for much longer. And the reason is the technologies are ready. You know, back in the 90s, we didn't get the cloud even until 2006. But there were visions of, you know, eyeballs in 10 years being the source of valuation today. We didn't get the cloud till or back then. We didn't get the cloud until 06. We didn't get the first big breakthrough in AI until deep learning, ImageNet, in 2012.

clips.shorts_title: Why So Many Investors Are Wrong About The AI Bubble
clips.description: Seasoned investors who lived through the dot-com bust are now the 'gray hairs' saying 'been there, done that' to the AI boom. But they're missing the point: this time, the technology is actually ready.
